title: Encoding roadmap
description: An enumeration of every unit of a subject's source text, each with a disposition, deposited BEFORE encoding begins and updated as it proceeds. It exists because P3's oracle is `l4 check` and nothing else: a module that encodes Chapter 1 and stops typechecks exactly as well as one that encodes the whole Act, so under-coverage is the pipeline's one large defect with no detector at all. The roadmap turns 'did we encode all of it' from an unfalsifiable judgement into a join, the way P1's annotation inventory turns 'did we dispose of every amendment' into one. It is not a plan the encoder may revise silently: a unit dropped from the enumeration is a change to what was promised, and reads as one.

encoding.description: The encoding id this roadmap is for. An occasion, not a position: the same source enumerated for two encodings gets two roadmaps, because scope is a decision of the job and not a property of the text.

granularity.description: The level units are counted at. Recorded because '100% of 12 chapters' and '100% of 400 subsections' are not the same claim, and a reader comparing two subjects cannot tell which they are reading without it.

document_id.description: The P1 source-bundle document this enumerates. Enumerating from memory rather than from the captured text is the failure this artifact exists to catch, so the id is joined against the bundle.

enumeration_basis.description: HOW the unit list was obtained, in a sentence a reader can repeat: 'every line matching ^[0-9]+\\. in source/PAA1934.txt', 'the Act's own arrangement-of-sections table at pp.1-3'. An enumeration nobody can re-derive is an assumption wearing an inventory's clothes.

enumeration_complete.description: True asserts this is every unit of the document at the stated granularity. False obliges enumeration_note. The flag exists so that 'I could not enumerate all of it' is a sayable answer, and nobody has to choose between overclaiming and stopping.

enumeration_note.description: Required when enumeration_complete is false: what the enumeration is missing, and why.

units.description: Every unit, in source order. Source order is load-bearing: it is what makes 'encoded 1 to 4, then nothing' visible at a glance in the rendered table, which is the exact failure this artifact was built for.

x-rules.description: No two units share an id. A duplicate id makes the coverage count meaningless and hides one of the two units from every join.
enumeration_complete false requires enumeration_note. An incomplete enumeration is legitimate; an unexplained one is a silent cap on what the roadmap can ever detect.

Dispositions out-of-scope and deferred require a reason of real length. 'Procedural machinery producing a fact the encoding takes as input' is a reason; 'not needed' is not. This is what makes a scope decision reviewable rather than merely recorded.
Dispositions encoded and inert require at least one module path. Without it the roadmap can only be checked against itself, and a unit can be marked encoded with nothing behind it.
Every module path a unit names must exist. Reported as a finding when the file is absent, so a roadmap cannot claim coverage in a module that was renamed or never written.
source.document_id must name a document the P1 source-bundle captured. Reported as skip when the bundle is not supplied, never silently passed.

id.description: The unit's citation as the source writes it: 's 13(2)', '227.100', 'Part 4'. Not a serial number, because the id is how a reader finds it in the text.

title.description: The source's own heading, quoted rather than paraphrased where it has one.

disposition.description: encoded: operative L4 exists. inert: carried as inert text, present but not active. out-of-scope: a deliberate decision not to encode, requiring a reason. deferred: intended and not done, requiring a reason — the status that makes an unfinished run say so out loud instead of looking finished.

modules.description: For encoded and inert: the module path(s) where the unit landed. What makes the roadmap checkable against the tree rather than only against itself.

anchor.description: Optional pinpoint into the module: a section name or a declaration name. Deliberately not a line number — line numbers move under every edit, and a stale anchor that still resolves is worse than none.
